stem:
Diya multiplies $(-3) \times 2 \times (-4) \times (-1)$.

Which claim about the sign of the product is correct?

options.text: The product is called a positive product because a product is being formed.
Negative signs pair away, so three negative factors still leave a positive product.
Three negative factors give a negative product.
The product is negative because $-3$ is the first factor written.

teacher.key_rationale: Count negative factors: three is odd, so the product is negative (−24). Calling any product "positive product" mislabels the sign test. Saying three negatives still yield positive reverses the odd/even rule. Blaming the first written factor conflates order with sign count.
